flagged.evidence: The Statement says “cofibrations are the maps with the left lifting property against the boundary maps.” Step 2.1 defines I as the free boundary inclusions, and Step 4.1 correctly defines Cof by LLP against I-injectives. In simplicial A-modules for nonzero A, I contains 0→A from ∂Δ[0]→Δ[0]; the square with both vertical maps 0→A, top 0→0, and bottom id_A has no diagonal A→0. Thus a generating cofibration does not have LLP against the boundary maps themselves.

[F1] repeats that cofibrations are maps with “the left lifting property against boundary maps.” The cited model-structure carrier defines cofibrations by LLP against boundary-injective maps; its boundary generator 0→A does not lift against itself (use bottom map id_A). This fact entry therefore states the same false characterization.

The text says a representable presheaf has the required value on the empty scheme “since Hom(∅,∅) is a one-point set.” For a representable presheaf h_X, the relevant value is Hom_S(∅,X); the displayed fact only checks h_∅ and does not by itself establish the claim for every representable. The claim is true because ∅ is initial, so this is a nonfatal notation/inference gap.
